title: In-Place Home Resale Vacant-Home Check and Home Alarms: Questions Answered
content:
**Rule.** Where an In-Place Home Resale package charges for the vacant-home check, the month's check charge carries an alarm credit that follows the home's alarm records: a monitored alarm on file with the seller's in-force Manufactured Home Insurance policy with Hearthstone credits 15.00; with no monitored alarm on file, a home whose model year on the seller's Home-Site Lease is 2015 or later credits 5.00; any other home credits nothing. The credit is subtracted from the month's visit charge as multiplied by any part-month rate; the remainder is never taken below zero and is rounded half up to the cent only at that final step.

| Monitored alarm on file with the in-force Manufactured Home Insurance policy | Model year on the Home-Site Lease | Alarm credit |
|---|---|---|
| yes | any | 15.00 |
| no | 2015 or later | 5.00 |
| no | 2014 or earlier | 0.00 |

## Questions answered by the rule

**Which insurance record counts?** The seller's Manufactured Home Insurance policy in in-force status, and whether a monitored alarm is on file with it.

**A 2019 home with a monitored alarm on file?** 15.00; the monitored alarm decides, and the two credits do not add up.

**A 2015 home with no monitored alarm on file?** 5.00.

**A 2014 home with no monitored alarm on file?** Nothing.

**A home whose Manufactured Home Insurance policy is not in force?** No monitored alarm is then on file with an in-force policy, so the credit follows the model year.

**A visit charge of 95.00 with a monitored alarm on file and no other credit?** 95.00 less 15.00 is 80.00.

(The homes and figures in these answers are hypothetical.)
